messages:
alex: heads up — found a batch of KMS-wrapped secrets in an old CI artifact snapshot (artifacts-prod-backups/2024-08). looks like they were wrapped with the old `ci-secrets-key` key version. not sure if the key was ever rotated properly.
jen (platform): ugh. are we confirmed that the ciphertext landed in a public place or just internal backups?
alex: internal backups only, but the backup bucket had overly permissive ACL for ~3 weeks last year. code fragment from the artifact: `ENC[KMS:v1:projects/rdw-prod/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/ci-secrets-key:Ci0xMjM0...]`
samir: that pattern matches our kms-wrapped env vars from the legacy pipeline. blast radius could include service accounts that had access to the kms key and any credentials stored in those artifacts.
maria (sec-oncall): paging the oncall: @maria (sec-oncall) — recommend we treat `ci-secrets-key` as potentially impacted. immediate actions: 1) disable old key version access, 2) identify affected service accounts and rotate their keys, 3) schedule secret re-ingestion (do not attempt bulk decrypt/rewrap without controls).
jen (platform): to be explicit — we should NOT run a mass decrypt/re-encrypt on the backup artifacts unless we have a safe enclave to handle plaintext. better to force rotation of secrets where possible (API keys, DB creds) and rotate service-account keys.
alex: agree. quick inventory commands I ran:
```
# list objects that contain ENC[KMS pattern (grep in gs)
gsutil ls gs://artifacts-prod-backups/** | xargs -n1 gsutil cat | rg "ENC\[KMS:v1" -n
```
samir: good. I'll run a scoped search across projects for `ENC[KMS:v1:projects/rdw-prod/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/ci-secrets-key` and produce a list of artifacts + owning repo.
maria (sec-oncall): ownership + impact matrix needed. we should tag each artifact with: project, repo, service-account(s) used during generation, and whether the secret is still active or already rotated. I'll take triage for prod-ops, alex you take legacy pipelines, jen take platform services. deadline: 4 hours.
jen (platform): for mitigation, I'm pushing an IAM deny binding on the key for all non-ops principals while we triage. command:
```
# sample gcloud deny (apply carefully)
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ci-secrets-key \
  --location=global --keyring=ci \
  --member='principalSet://goog/public:allAuthenticatedUsers' \
  --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter' 
```
(note: we'll craft exact members; doing a deny for encrypter/decrypter for everyone except the ops group)
alex: note: we also have Vault entries that reference these wrapped blobs (legacy vault paths `secret/ci/*`). vault-bot, can you enumerate vault paths that contain the `ENC[KMS` marker?
vault-bot: Found 12 paths under `secret/ci/legacy/` with `ENC[KMS:v1` pattern. Listing: secret/ci/legacy/backup1, backup2, backup3... (redacted).
maria (sec-oncall): perfect. next: communicate to teams to rotate credentials rather than rewrap ciphertext. steps: 1) create ticket per owning team to rotate secrets (link to rot-ticket-template), 2) disable service-account keys tied to artifacts, 3) revoke any active short-lived tokens issued from those SAs.
samir: for DB passwords we can trigger password rotation via the credential manager API. for API keys we need owners to generate new keys and flip runtime env vars. I'll prepare a playbook snippet.
jen (platform): update deploy pipelines to reject `ENC[KMS` artifacts — pipeline lint change I can push. Also add an explicit step to fail if a workspace contains raw wrapped ciphers in artifacts.
alex: one more thing — audit logs. I noticed an audit gap for KMS Decrypt on key version 3 between 2024-07-01 and 2024-07-10. we should preserve logs and escalate to cloud support if needed. samir, can you pull Cloud Audit Logs for `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` for that interval?
samir: on it. will export logs to a read-only bucket and share link.
maria (sec-oncall): owners and action items recap: alex — inventory legacy vault paths + open rotation tickets (due +4h). jen — apply temporary deny on key + pipeline lint (due +2h). samir — artifact & audit log search + SA key revocations (due +3h). vault-bot — mark affected vault entries as "stale-exposed" tag. I'll follow up with an incident summary and notify compliance.
jen (platform): one caveat — some long-lived services (billing export, metrics) rely on the old encryption workflow. before deny we should whitelist the infra ops SA and the migration workers. I'll add those principals to the allowlist in the deny policy.
alex: agreed. once tickets are created, we should rotate secrets in this order: 1) DB credentials, 2) service-account JSON keys, 3) third-party API keys, 4) internal app tokens. include rollback plan and config change windows.
maria (sec-oncall): launching post-incident channel #sec-incident-ci-kms-2024 for coordination and compliance notes. I'll paste the summary and timeline there. if anyone finds evidence of external access to that backup bucket, mark priority P1 and escalate to legal.
samir: sharing initial artifact list in the channel in 30m.
jen (platform): pushing deny now (with whitelist). will follow up with CL for pipeline lint.
alex: thanks. will start ticketing and reach out to repo owners.
maria (sec-oncall): good work team. keep updates short and tag with #ci-kms-leak.
